Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
904 AM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Coverage of showers and a few thunderstorms may be a bit higher
later today. A Coastal Flood Advisory has been issued for this 
afternoon's high tide at Annapolis. The Small Craft Advisory was
extended until 3 AM for the wider waters off southern Maryland.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Remaining warm with renewed rain chances through Friday. 

- 2) Seasonably cool temperatures and mountain rain showers 
  this weekend; drying out with high pressure next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Remaining warm with renewed rain chances through 
Friday.

Synoptically, a broad upper-level trough over the northern/eastern
Great Lakes will eject northeast into southern Ontario through 
Friday. At the surface is a lead shortwave trough/cold front which
looks to cross the area through this afternoon. Most shower 
activity was diminishing as of mid morning for the time being.

Latest runs of the RAP, HRRR and RRFS/REFS hint at a bit more
shower and thunderstorm coverage a couple hours earlier east of
the Blue Ridge/Catoctin Mountains by mid to late afternoon.

By tonight, the front stalls somewhere along and east of I-95. The 
front will lead to a steadier/heavier slug of rain across areas east 
of the Blue Ridge (in particular southern MD/northern neck of VA).
This is due largely in part to a wave of low pressure that will
develop along the front combined with a narrow band of low-level
convergence as a jet streak develops (forces modest moisture 
advection) overhead. Current guidance shows good agreement in 
regards to the timing and placement of the boundary yielding 
rain amounts on the order of 0.75-1.25" across southern MD and 
the northern neck of VA. Locally higher totals up to 2" are 
possible over extreme southern MD and northern neck of VA given 
the track of the low as it pushes through. No flooding is 
expected given the 2+ week hiatus of measurable rainfall and 
ongoing drought concerns. Locations along and just east of I-95 
will see rain amounts between a 0.25-0.50" but the locally 1"+
amounts will be very close. Meanwhile, locations further west 
will see less given downsloping effects.

The front and upper-level trough kick offshore Friday evening 
into Saturday morning yielding drier conditions. Upslope rain 
showers and perhaps a few snowflakes will linger over the 
Alleghenies within northwest flow. These rain showers won't 
amount to a whole lot as another wave of energy passes north of 
the region.

The big thing to note will be the temperatures. Above normal highs 
in the low to mid 70s are expected today with mid 60s and low 70s 
Friday. These values cool into the 50s and mid 60s this weekend with 
mountain highs only in the 40s. A colder airmass sweeps in behind
the front/trough Friday night as lows drop to the upper 30s to 
upper 40s.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Seasonably cool temperatures and mountain rain 
showers this weekend; drying out with high pressure next week. 

The first trough of low pressure and front will depart the area 
Saturday morning with another upper-level disturbance set to 
pass to the north Saturday and Sunday. This disturbance will 
bring upslope showers and perhaps a few flakes to the 
Alleghenies with passing clouds further east. Conditions will 
remain breezy out of the west and northwest with gusts between 
20 to 30 mph. Temperatures will also be noticeably cooler with 
highs in the 50s and low 60s Saturday and low to mid 60s Sunday.
Overnight lows will fall back into the 30s and 40s.

A weakened cold front will push across the region Monday morning 
with a warm front set to push into the area Tuesday. This will be 
followed by a stronger front mid to late week bringing back the 
"True Fall" air to the region. Conditions will remain dry 
overall as high pressure builds in from the southeastern U.S. 
Tuesday through Thursday next week (in a zonal flow pattern 
aloft). Highs will range from the low to mid 60s Monday to upper
60s and low 70s Tuesday as the warm front passes through. Highs
will sink back into the 50s and low 60s midweek. Overnight lows
will remain in the 30s and 40s. Winds will decrease midweek 
leading to potential frost and freeze conditions toward the I-95
metros where the growing season continues.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Pockets of MVFR CIGs are expected this morning as a cold front 
pushes into the region. A lull in shower activity with gradually
lifting CIGs is expected this afternoon and evening. VFR to 
MVFR conditions are expected this afternoon and evening as the 
front slowly stalls over/east the I-95 corridor. Winds will 
remain out of the south and southwest today at 10 to 15 kts with
gusts up to 20 kts during the late morning and early afternoon 
period. Winds will lighten tonight while remaining out of the 
west and south at 5 to 10 kts. Highest gusts will be at 
terminals near the waters and along the terrain ahead of/behind 
the immediate frontal passage. May add PROB30s as confidence in
coverage for showers and a few t-storms is increasing mid
afternoon into the evening east of the Blue Ridge.

Another round of low clouds and rain shower activity is expected 
late tonight into Friday afternoon. The heaviest rain looks to be 
just east of the I-95 corridor terminals. Even with that said, the 
potential for low CIGs and VSBYs remain, especially at terminals
east of a line from MRB to CHO. The front and wave of low 
pressure moves offshore late Friday night into Saturday yielding
gradually improving conditions. Winds will transition to the 
north and northwest at 5 to 15 kts.

VFR conditions Saturday through Monday. Winds northwest 10 to 20 
knots gusts 25 knots generally in the period. A cold front passes 
Monday morning with a warm front Tuesday leading to another wind 
shift across the region. Remaining VFR through the middle of 
next week as high pressure builds to the south.

&&

.MARINE...
A cold front is set to slowly move across the waters through Friday. 
Ahead of the front will be a period of southerly channeling with 
gusts 20-25 kts, though may be somewhat sporadic depending on
vertical mixing and channeling effects. Small Craft Advisories 
remain in effect to encompass this threat through this evening,
and have been extended over the wider waters off southern MD
into the overnight. Winds diminish heading into Friday with the
cold front sweeping through Friday evening. SCA conditions are 
likely in the wake of the front Friday night into Saturday. 
Widespread rain chances will accompany the front with some 
heavier showers and perhaps a few t-storms over the open waters 
as low pressure passes overhead tonight into Friday.

Small Craft Advisories are likely Saturday and Sunday, and are 
possible on Monday. Winds northwest 15 to 20 knots gusts 25 to 
30 knots.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies this morning are running around 1 to 1.5 feet. 
Expect these to continue to gradually rise in response to 
southerly flow ahead of a cold front. This will bring a few 
locations into Action stage through this afternoon before water 
levels drop behind the departing cold front. Annapolis appears
on track to hit minor flooding for this afternoon's high tide,
and Alexandria and Havre de Grace may be close early this
evening as well.

&&
